title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (May 2026)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Executive summary:

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (MVP + milestones), high-level design specs, roadmap & themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and the initial release notes for Unified Inference (May 2026 release). It is intended for product, engineering, and GTM stakeholders preparing for GA and enterprise enablement.

1) Product overview

- Goal: Provide a single, consistent inference API and operational model across Hosted (API), Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments that optimizes for latency, cost, and reliability.
- Primary users: ML engineers, backend engineers, platform teams.
- Key product pillars: runtime performance, predictable economics, deployment flexibility, and observability.

2) Goals and success metrics

- Business goals:
  - Drive PLG adoption by reducing integration time to <30 mins for quickstarts.
  - Convert power users to Dedicated contracts with an initial uplift target of 12% of active orgs in 6 months.
- Product/technical goals:
  - 99th-percentile inference latency <120ms for small-chat workloads on hosted small-tier models.
  - 15% reduction in per-token cost vs previous baseline via batching + caching recommendations.
  - 99.9% availability for Dedicated customers under committed capacity.
- Success metrics (KPIs): adoption rate, conversion to Dedicated, average per-token cost, latency percentiles, number of regressions detected by quality monitoring.

3) PRD — MVP feature set (must-haves)

- Unified REST/SDK endpoints with: generate, chat, embeddings, reranking.
- Model catalog driven by versioned artifacts; simple pin-by-version workflow.
- Smart routing policy: latency-first, cost-first, and tenant-priority presets.
- Built-in prefix/KV caching with per-customer cache configs.
- Observability: per-route token-level cost, latency breakdowns, and rollout trace.
- Rollouts: canary percentage control, A/B variant, automatic fallback to model variants.

Non-goals (MVP exclusions):
- Full multi-cloud scheduler for Private on-prem autoscaling.
- Fine-grained per-request language detection routing.

4) Requirements (epics & acceptance criteria)

- Epic: Core API parity
  - Req: SDK parity for Python/Go/Node for generate/chat/embeddings.
  - Acceptance: sample quickstart completes end-to-end in <30 minutes.

- Epic: Model catalog and versioning
  - Req: Catalog supports semantic version + immutable artifact hash.
  - Acceptance: model rollbacks restore previous behavior within 2 minutes and preserve KV compatibility notes.

- Epic: Observability & Cost controls
  - Req: Token-level cost export to billing + per-route dashboards.
  - Acceptance: cost drilldown available in Console and matches billing exports to within 1%.

5) High-level design/specs

- Architecture overview:
  - Control plane (central): rollout/traffic policies, catalog, billing integration, Console UI.
  - Data plane (region/tenant): runtime serving, KV cache, batching, quantization profiles.
  - Smart router: policy engine that selects data plane target based on latency/cost/region.

- Interfaces and contracts:
  - API: OpenAPI 3.0 compatible; request/response schema documented.
  - SDKs: stable client with retry/backoff semantics; 0-downtime token auth rotation.

- Config table (example):
  | config_key | description | allowed_values | default | owner |
  | batching.max_tokens | Max tokens per batch | integer (>=1) | 2048 | eng-serving-runtime |
  | routing.policy | Routing preset | latency|cost|region | latency | eng-platform |
  | cache.ttl_secs | KV cache TTL per-tenant | integer seconds | 300 | eng-infra |

- Example API (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-unified-1.0", "input":"Summarize the following...", "max_tokens":256}'

6) Roadmap & themes (quarterly view)

- Q2 2026 (May–Jun) — GA release (this doc):
  - GA for Hosted API with Unified endpoints; Console dashboards (cost+latency); MVP routing presets; SDK parity.
  - Release notes: see section 9.
- Q3 2026 — Dedicated expansion:
  - Reserved capacity SKU + SLA pricing, burst capacity controls, dedicated autoscaler.
- Q4 2026 — Private & compliance:
  - VPC control plane GA, on-prem packaging, KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2 re-audit.
- Q1 2027 — Optimization & quality:
  - Redwood Optimize v4 integration (auto-quant recommendations), eval-driven regression detection, prompt-set monitoring.

Strategic themes: performance-first, predictable economics, enterprise readiness, developer friction reduction.

7) Pricing & packaging notes (guidance for GTM)

- Hosted API (PLG): usage-based pricing (tokens + embeddings). Introduce tiered commit credits to encourage Dedicated trials.
  - Starter (free tier): 0–10k generation tokens/day, community support.
  - Professional: pay-as-you-go at published rates, priority support.
  - Enterprise (Dedicated): commit-based monthly pricing, SLA add-ons, volume discounts.

- Pricing levers: model complexity, sequence length, quantization profiles, cache hits metric (lower unit cost for high cache-hit customers).

- Packaging: bundle Console observability (basic) with all tiers; premium observability retention and compliance add-ons sold separately.

8) Release plan & rollout (GA May 2026)

- Release windows: staged rollout over 5 days by region (US-EAST -> US-WEST -> EU -> APAC).
- Canary plan: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks at each stage (latency, error-rate, cost anomalies).
- Health checks and thresholds:
  - Latency: 95p not increased >10% vs baseline.
  - Errors: 5xx rate <0.1% sustained.
  - Cost anomalies: per-tenant cost delta <20% vs sample baseline; flag for investigation.

9) Release notes (May 2026 GA)

- New: Unified REST/SDK endpoints for generate, chat, embeddings, and reranking.
- New: Versioned model catalog with pin-by-version workflow.
- New: Console: per-route token-level cost, latency breakdowns, rollout controls.
- Improvements: default batching & KV caching enabled for Hosted; expected per-token cost reduction median 12%.
- Known issues:
  - Private on-prem installer does not yet support automated hardware discovery (workaround: manual inventory).
  - Small percentage of models require manual kernel selection on older GPU drivers; eng-serving-runtime is triaging.

10) Rollout ownership, support, and escalation

- Release owner: Priya Desai (product).
- Engineering leads: Michael Chen (serving runtime), Noor Patel (platform & routing), Daniel Ruiz (observability).
- Support escalation matrix: on-call SRE -> eng-serving-runtime -> product owner. See related runbooks: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/rollout-escalation.

11) Open risks and mitigations

- Risk: Unexpected cost spikes from naive batching defaults. Mitigation: conservative defaults + cost guardrails and throttles; pre-release billing simulation for top 50 tenants.
- Risk: Model quality regressions after rollout. Mitigation: eval suite + auto-regression alerts tied to prompt sets; canary traffic routed to stable variants.

12) Next steps & action items

- Engineering: complete SDK parity tests and end-to-end quickstart (owner: Michael Chen) — target 2026-05-07.
- Product: finalize pricing tiers & published docs (owner: Ava Martinez) — target 2026-05-04.
- GTM: prepare enablement slide deck + pricing guidance (owner: Liam O'Connor) — target 2026-05-08.
